From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap:
- Goal: validate Redwood's hosted endpoint for your Customer Assist feature under production-like load.
- Success criteria (from the call): p95 latency <= 300ms for 1k token responses, sustained throughput of ~500 req/s with bursts to 2k req/s, concurrency ~200 active streams, and stable streaming chunk latencies for server-sent events.

Open items we asked you to confirm: 
1) Preferred test window (timezone): you mentioned Mar 3–4 evenings PT; can you confirm an exact 4-hour window?
2) Test accounts / tokens: we'll need 1 read-only test API key + 1 workload account that can generate streaming responses.
3) IP allowlist: please provide the client IP ranges we should allow for your k6/Locust agents.
4) Load test artifact: if you can share the k6/Locust script (or a representative subset), we can pre-run locally to validate request shapes.

Proposed next steps (our side):
- Once we receive the script and IPs, our SRE (cc'd) will provision the test account and add allowlist entries.
- We'll run a brief smoke ramp on Mar 2 to verify auth/paths.
- Customer-led test on your confirmed window; Redwood will monitor and provide live token/latency breakdowns and post-test logs.

Attachments you can send: k6 or Locust script, an example payload file, and the list of IPs. If you prefer, drop them into the Drive link I shared (or reply here).

Thanks — looking forward to the test.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming details from our side: 

SLOs & Traffic shape (confirmed):
- p95 end-to-end latency target: <= 300ms (for responses up to ~1,000 tokens); p99 ideally < 800ms.
- Sustained throughput: 500 req/s; 5-minute sustained bursts up to 2,000 req/s.
- Concurrency: typical production concurrency target ~200 concurrent sessions; test should exercise up to 250 to provide headroom.
- Streaming: client expects server-side events with chunking every ~150ms under steady state; we need to validate chunk latencies.

Test window: prefer Wed Mar 3, 20:00–24:00 PT (we can shift an hour earlier if necessary).

IP allowlist (agent egress):
- 35.199.32.0/21
- 34.82.0.0/15
(we're running agents from GCP us-west1)

Attached is our baseline k6 script (acme_k6_script.js) and a sample payload. We'll also provide a Locust variant if you prefer. For credentials, please provision a scoped test key that only hits the public inference endpoints and doesn't touch sensitive customer data.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_k6_script.js (application/javascript)]

Let me know if the window works and once the test account is ready we'll go ahead and start.

Thanks,
Sofia Reyes
Senior Product Manager — Customer Assist

- Provision a scoped test API key (scopes: inference:read, inference:stream) and create a short-lived workload account for Acme.
- Add egress allowlist for 35.199.32.0/21 and 34.82.0.0/15 to the staging ingress rules for the hosted endpoint.
- Validate that our hosted pool can sustain 2k rps bursts with 250 concurrency for a 4-hour window; if not, advise on Dedicated fallback or rate-limit plans.

Can you confirm by EOD that the test account will be ready and whether we need any capacity changes? HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-EXP-2027-03

Marissa
